description: Whole and damp, a brown iris in a veined tan ball. The fiends that carry spares will not miss this one.
lore: Whole or worth nothing. That is the first hard lesson of the trade and it gets learned on these, because they are the commonest eye out there and sixteen gold is real money to someone on a first bag. A burst one is a wet mark on a cloth. So you learn the spoon — the shape of it, the angle, exactly how much you can hurry and where you cannot — and you learn it at night, at the edge of a fire, from somebody who has already finished their own bag and could be asleep.

Everyone in the trade can tell you who taught them the spoon. Not the first buyer who paid them properly, not the crossing where they lost a boot: the person who sat back down in the cold with someone else's leavings and showed them how. [[lore/the_hard_pieces|Both of the trade's words]] get used about this work, and neither of them covers that.
gm_notes: The apprenticeship record: the ugliest task in the trade is also where its one reliable kindness lives. Any veteran NPC can be asked who taught them the spoon and will answer, at once, with a name.
